en: The single bilva fruit—having three lobes, the form of the three qualities, three eyes, and the three weapons—is the destroyer of the sins of the three births when offered to Śiva. 1.
With three-pronged bilva leaves—unblemished, tender, and auspicious—I shall perform your worship; a single bilva leaf is offered to Śiva. (2)
Beholding the bilva tree brings about the destruction of sin through touch;
a single bilva fruit offered to Śiva effects the eradication of even the most terrible sins. (3)
Dwelling in the sacred field of Kāśī, beholding Kālabhairava, seeing Mādhava at Prayāga, and offering a single bilva fruit to Śiva; || 4 ||
Tulasī, Bilva, Nirguṇḍī, Jambīra, and likewise Āmalaka—
these are known as the "Five Bilvas," while a single Bilva is an offering to Śiva.
A pond, the depositing of wealth, a sanctuary established for Brahmins, a temple of Śiva, the great gift of ten million virgins, and a single bilva fruit offered to Śiva—[these are equal]. (6)
The gift of ten million elephants and horses, hundreds of horse-sacrifices, and the great gift of ten million maidens are all equaled by a single bilva fruit offered to Śiva. (7)
A thousand Śālagrāmas, a hundred billion offerings of food to Brahmins, and thousands of millions of sacrifices are all equaled by a single Bilva fruit offered to Śiva. (8)
Whatever sin has been committed through ignorance, and whatever has been committed even with knowledge—may all that go to destruction through this single bilva fruit offered to Śiva. 9.
With each individual bilva leaf, one obtains the fruit of ten million sacrifices.
For the sake of worshipping Mahādeva, even a single bilva leaf offered to Śiva [yields this result]. (10)
From the tree born of nectar, which is dear to Mahādeva, men are indeed released from the wounds of thorns by means of the thorns themselves. 11.
